title: End-of-page menu morph follows your scroll instead of locking it (phones)
problem: At the end of the page, on a phone, the page takes over your scroll: once you reach the bottom, it cancels your finger's moves, pins the page in place every frame, and plays a 680 ms spring that grows the small nav pill into the dark panel (the 'morph'). Your finger stops scrolling the page for that moment.
idea: On touch phones only, the page gets one extra screen of scroll after the last section. The last section (#platform) stays put (CSS sticky) while that screen scrolls in, and the morph value is simply how far it has scrolled in, 0 to 1. So the panel opens and closes with your finger, like a normal scroll. Nothing cancels touch moves, nothing pins the page, no spring runs. Light snapping (CSS scroll-snap 'proximity') pulls a rest near closed or near open to the end. Built on the best build B-R2 plus the morph-on-GPU change (morph-gpu rev 2 A) and its early layer prep. Desktop, tablets and reduced motion keep today's behaviour. Base (A): js 8018ce062d30, css 71b65c667720; this (B): js 9834ccf0a643, css b829d8e7ae29.
looksSame: No. The motion is new: the panel follows the finger instead of a fixed spring, and it can rest half open (see the differences). Still frames at the same morph value match the base in Chrome and, while the panel covers the last section, in the iOS Simulator (only the running countdown differs, in A vs A too). Where the last section shows, Safari draws its text about 1 device pixel higher (T3, below).
visualDiff: Motion: the morph follows your scroll position, not a 680 ms spring. Scroll halfway and the panel is halfway open.

Half-open rest is possible: Safari snaps a 'proximity' point only within 0.3 of the screen height (WebKit source, CONFIRMED), so a rest between about 30 % and 70 % open stays there. Option if you want it: settle to the nearer end when the finger lets go (not built).

Safari only, T3 (over the wide rule by share, not by shade): wherever the last section (#platform) is on screen, its text and edges sit about 1 device pixel (1/3 CSS px) higher. Closed at the end: 0.89 % of the screen over 8 shades, max 77. One screen before: 0.57 %, max 78. Base vs base: 0.
Why (Safari): the box position is identical to 1/64 px. WebKit gives every sticky box its own GPU layer (WebKit source, CONFIRMED); that this layer causes the 1 px shift is OBSERVED, cause unknown.
Safari, panel covering the section (m 0.25 to 1): equal to the base apart from the countdown, which also differs base vs base (max shade 224 in both).
Chrome: within the base-vs-base noise at every morph value, except the EN language label at the top right (about 300 device px, also seen base vs base in a second run).
The page is one screen longer on phones.
Nothing changes on desktop, tablets or with reduced motion.

gain.what: Touch moves cancelled at the end of the page
gain.how: By the code: under the phone gate the listener is never added. Checked in Chrome; the Simulator check scrolled by script only.

gain.what: Per-frame scroll pin and spring loop during the morph
gain.how: By the code and the Simulator scroll-step check (31 steps: morph value = scroll position, section held at the screen bottom every step).

gain.what: Smoothness and feel on the iPhone
gain.how: Needs a phone ticket and your blind swipe A/B (timing is deferred). Also untested: Safari's toolbar collapsing mid-scroll, and whether the scroll callback runs every frame during a finger scroll.

risk: A motion change: you decide whether the end-of-page morph should follow the finger. A half-open rest can happen (WebKit's snap range, CONFIRMED). In Safari the last section is drawn 1 device px higher wherever it shows (T3), and it is its own GPU layer for the whole visit (memory not measured). Checked only with scripted scrolls in Chrome and the iOS Simulator, with the toolbar shown; no finger or gesture run yet, no reduced motion in Safari, no iPad, no rubber-band check. It reuses fix-nav-morph's setter and gate and morph-gpu rev 2 A: if accepted it becomes a conflict cluster with nav-morph and is rebuilt on top of nav-morph's landed version, and the nav-hit-cache change would need one extra line (__nsForce) to keep the nav colour right.
